name: manybody-sign-by-bond-topology
description: The many-body term at fixed nucleon content is exactly zero on chains, positive for the A=3 triangle in all six orders, and negative for the A=4 complete graph in every order tried; even the complete graph reaches only 10.08 MeV against AME 28.296.
scope: (a) A=4 orderings sampled (3 of 720), A=3 exhaustive. Pure chains, not nuclei. Nothing fitted or wired.

assertions.name: single-bond L is independent of separation, to 1e-40
assertions.detail: max deviation 1.47002e-50 across all six pairs. The t7qv witness reports this as 3.4e-13 by a float64 route; measured here in mpmath it holds to 1.47e-50 — an independent implementation confirming their result thirty-seven orders of magnitude tighter.

assertions.name: two-bond sets are EXACTLY additive; the triangle is POSITIVE in all six orders
assertions.detail: pairs: max |many-body| 1.336e-51 — exactly zero, band-routed included, so two bonds commute. Triangle: all six orders positive, range 0.0745689 to 0.181007. A positive many-body term DOES exist.

assertions.name: at A=4 every complete-graph order is NEGATIVE, and the chain is exactly zero
assertions.detail: K4 many-body: -1.07346, -0.560713, -0.530718 — all negative. Chain: 5.346e-51, exactly zero, confirming bond-additivity on the adjacent set. So the sign FLIPS between A=3 and A=4 and is negative exactly where the alpha particle lives.

assertions.name: the non-additive route is short by ~2.8x, so neither route reaches the alpha
assertions.detail: 2.80636x short. Additive was capped at 20.649 MeV (1.37x short) with free per-bond values; non-additive with every interference term reaches 10.082684 MeV. Both closed.

assertions.name: the definitional difference from t7qv is stated, not glossed
assertions.detail: Fixed-nucleon-content vs subset-Mobius are different quantities. Reporting the sign disagreement without naming the definitional difference would misrepresent their result as an error.
